heroHeadline: TTP Kills 15+ Police in Bannu Car Bomb + Drone Attack on Day 74; Karzai Warns Tribal Ceasefire Deals Risk Legitimizing Durand Line
heroSubtitle: On May 10, 2026 (Day 74 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), TTP-linked militants from the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan alliance and Hafiz Gul Bahadar group struck the Fateh Khel police checkpost in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with a suicide car bomb, armed assault, and quadcopter drones — killing at least 15 police officers. The attack, staged from North Waziristan sanctuaries bordering Afghanistan, is one of the deadliest single-incident TTP strikes on Pakistani law enforcement in 2026 and directly illustrates Pakistan's rationale for sustaining Operation Ghazab lil-Haq: that Afghan-based TTP sanctuaries continue enabling mass-casualty attacks on Pakistani soil even during the fragile inter-state tactical pause. On May 9 (Day 73), former Afghan President Hamid Karzai warned that Pakistan's formal endorsement of tribal ceasefire deals between Bajaur-Kunar and Nuristan-Chitral border communities represents 'an attempt by Pakistan to legitimise the so-called Durand Line' — a claim that strikes at the core of Afghan sovereignty and the unresolved border dispute. The Afghan Taliban government has not commented on the Bannu attack, the Karzai statement, or the tribal ceasefire arrangements. No formal ceasefire has been signed between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban government, no Urumqi Round 2 date has been set, and China has remained publicly silent since the May 5 Dangam civilian strike.
